newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Norilsk to restructure government debts.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Norilsk to restructure government debts.

text.p: Russian metals mining group Norilsk Nickel will restructure its debt to the government by mutual debt cancellation and new share issues, a spokeswoman for the privatisation minister said on Friday.

Viktoriya Vergelskaya, spokeswoman for Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh who heads the State Property Committee, told Reuters Norilsk's subsidiaries owed the federal government over 1.3 trillion roubles ($225 million) on June 1.

She said 600 billion roubles ($104.1 million) would be restructured with Norilsk combine, the group's main plant, through mutual debt forgiveness, as the federal government owed the firm for precious metals shipments.
The remaining 700 billion roubles ($121.4 million) would be restructured according to a government programme.
Norilsk combine will issue new shares covering 50 percent plus one share of equity to be held by the government against arrears payment over 10 years.
"Arrears of other companies (controlled by Norilsk Nickel) will be restructured according to the same scheme," she said.
A government order on the restructuring will be finished next week, she said.
Vergelskaya said another 1.5 trillion roubles ($260.2 million) which Norilsk subsidiaries owe the Pension Fund would be paid off in five years.
A further 1.6 trillion roubles ($277.6 million) owed to the local administration would be worked out separately, she said.
Norilsk Nickel spokesman Anatoly Komrakov told Reuters earlier the firm owed over 6.7 trillion roubles ($1.16 billion) on June 1.
